In [[mathematics]], '''Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue''' is, as of 2018, an unsolved [[conjecture]] proposed by [[Shing-Tung Yau]] in 1982. It asks:

<blockquote>Is it true that the first [[eigenvalue]] for the [[Laplace–Beltrami operator]] on an embedded closed [[minimal surface|minimal]] [[hypersurface]] of <math>S^{n+1}</math> is <math>n</math>?</blockquote>

If true, it will imply that the area of embedded minimal hypersurfaces in <math>S^3</math> will have an upper bound depending only on the [[genus (mathematics)|genus]]. The Yau's conjecture is verified for several special cases, but still [[open problem|open]] in general.

[[Chern's conjecture for hypersurfaces in spheres|Shiing-Shen Chern conjectured]] that a closed, minimally immersed hypersurface in <math>S^{n+1}</math>(1), whose [[second fundamental form]] has constant length, is isoparametric. If true, it would have established the Yau's conjecture for the minimal hypersurface whose second fundamental form has constant length.

A possible generalization of the Yau's conjecture:

<blockquote>Let <math>M^d</math> be a closed minimal submanifold in the unit sphere <math>S^{N+1}</math>(1) with dimension <math>d</math> of <math>M^d</math> satisfying <math>d \ge 2n/3 + 1</math>. Is it true that the first eigenvalue of <math>M^d</math> is <math>d</math>?</blockquote>
